recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Latvia sending about 20 soldiers to the Strait of Hormuz was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. This one was a genuine deployment, not a keyword-matching error like the wildfire correction below — but it's Latvia's own contribution to an international coalition maritime security mission on the other side of the world, with no connection to Russia or the Baltic region. The scoring gap that let this through (a Baltic country's own unrelated foreign deployments passing as a Baltic security signal) has been fixed. As always, the false positive stays in the historical record rather than being quietly deleted.
recent_corrections.context: Latvia plans to send about 20 soldiers to Strait of Hormuz — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-04

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Lithuania sending firefighters to help France fight wildfires was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. Cause: a scoring bug — generic words like 'deployed' and 'reinforcements' (meant to catch real troop movements) were also matching ordinary disaster-response language. That bug, and several similar ones found in a full audit of the scoring keywords, has been fixed. The false positive stays in the historical record below rather than being quietly deleted — see our policy on this.
recent_corrections.context: Lithuania sends 32 firefighters to help France fight wildfires — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-01

recent_updates.title: New: Composite Escalation Index -- a public trend line, not a prediction
recent_updates.text: Owner-requested: "we are not predicting the future... we are tracking escalation and measure it." Added a new composite measurement built entirely from four numbers this project already computes every scan -- each Tier-1 signal's own deviation-from-trailing-baseline percentage (GPS-jamming, AIS vessels, military aircraft, FIRMS thermal hotspots; compute_gpsjam_deviation()/compute_ais_deviation()/compute_military_deviation()/compute_firms_deviation()). Those four were previously only computed on a WATCH/WARN scan, purely to build a digest context line -- now computed on EVERY scan (pure math over history already recorded, no extra fetch), and compute_composite_escalation_index() averages whichever of the four currently have a valid baseline (at least 2 of 4 required, each clamped to +/-300% before averaging so one noisy source can't dominate) into one number: how far today's readings sit from normal, across independently-verified signals. Persisted every scan to a new escalation_index_history.json (mirroring gpsjam/ais/military/firms_history.json exactly) and published via generate_public_chart_data()'s new escalation_index_points array. Deliberately NOT a probability, a prediction, or a replacement for the corroboration-gated WARN/WATCH/QUIET trigger in score_and_group(), which this never touches -- same 'show the real data, say plainly what it isn't' posture as /satellite's refusal to do ML change-detection. On the site: a new prominent widget right after the hero showing the current reading plus 'N of 4 signals elevated', and a full history chart in the Track record section alongside the other five. 13 new tests (616 -> 629).

recent_updates.title: Bluesky added as a fourth public alert channel
recent_updates.text: Added Bluesky (AT Protocol) as a fourth, Telegram-independent public alert channel, mirroring the existing Mastodon channel exactly: only an actual WATCH/WARN or a recovery back to QUIET, never routine QUIET scans or the weekly/daily/trend reports, same plain-text 'quick alert, link to site' shape (now shared between both via a common _format_short_alert_post() helper), just re-capped to Bluesky's tighter 300-grapheme post limit instead of Mastodon's ~500-character one. Unlike Mastodon's static bearer token, Bluesky's API is session-based -- each post authenticates fresh via com.atproto.server.createSession then writes the post via com.atproto.repo.createRecord, both endpoint shapes confirmed against real, current lexicon docs and a live request before writing any code. A fresh session per post (no caching) is deliberate and safe: this only fires on infrequent real alerts, and Bluesky's own documented rate limit (30 createSession calls per 5 minutes, 300/day) leaves huge headroom. Auth is a Bluesky App Password (Settings -> App Passwords on bsky.app), never the main account password. New secrets: BLUESKY_HANDLE and BLUESKY_APP_PASSWORD; posting cleanly no-ops until both are set. Its on-demand test command (test_bluesky) deliberately never writes a public post -- Bluesky has no Mastodon-style private/followers-only visibility to fall back on, so it only verifies session creation, confirming the credentials work without ever showing test noise on the public timeline. No PII collected, no scoring changes. 19 new tests (597 -> 616).

recent_updates.title: New: four more public-site charts -- GPS-jamming, AIS, military aircraft, FIRMS
recent_updates.text: Owner-requested: 'more graphs like estwarden had.' The public site's Track record section already had two charts (escalation intensity, rumor/disinfo tracking); this adds four more using data already collected every scan but never charted publicly -- GPS-jamming intensity (gpsjam_history.json), AIS vessel counts (ais_history.json), military aircraft counts (military_history.json), and NASA FIRMS thermal hotspot counts (firms_history.json), the same four sources the map entry above already tracks as aggregate counts. generate_public_chart_data() now exports gpsjam_points/ais_points/military_points/firms_points (each a plain {ts, count} array) alongside the existing points array, still in the same public_chart_data.json -- no new published file needed. GPS-jamming is recorded once per calendar day (not per scan), so its date field is mapped to midnight UTC that day rather than reused verbatim. On the site, renderRumorChart()'s bar-chart logic was generalized into a reusable renderCountChart() so all five count-style series (rumors plus the four new ones) share one renderer instead of four more copy-pasted chart functions -- four new chart blocks inside the existing range-selector section, each with its own honestly-caveated caption, translated across EN/ET/LV/LT. 5 new tests (592 -> 597).

recent_updates.title: New: a real map on the public site (AIS, military aircraft, GPS jamming, thermal hotspots)
recent_updates.text: Closes the last piece of the estwarden.eu competitive gap named in the FIRMS/satellite entries above: this project already fetched real positions every scan for AIS ships, military ADS-B aircraft, GPSJam H3 cells, and FIRMS thermal hotspots, but only ever persisted aggregate COUNTS (ais_history.json/military_history.json/gpsjam_history.json/firms_history.json) -- never the actual lat/lon points, so none of it was ever plotted anywhere. record_map_positions() now records a bounded, pruned rolling window (72h, documented in main.py alongside every other constant) of real positions across all four sources to a new map_positions.json, reusing whatever run_scan() already fetched for the existing count-based Phase 2 blocks -- no duplicate fetching. generate_public_map_data() (same pattern as generate_public_status_json()/generate_public_chart_data()) publishes a small, capped slice (150 points/layer max) to public_map_data.json, copied to the public site repo as map_data.json by scan.yml, same mechanism as status.json/chart_data.json. GPSJam cells are deduped by (hex, date) and FIRMS hotspots by (lat, lon, acq_date, acq_time) so re-fetching the same underlying detection across consecutive scans does not write duplicate points; AIS/military positions are never deduped, since every scan there is a genuinely fresh live sample and repeat points are what let the map show real movement. Same trust posture as everywhere else this data appears: not curated, self-declared/spoofable where applicable, purely informational, never itself a trigger -- this only changes the PRESENTATION of data already collected every scan and already shared with the owner via Telegram, not what is collected. The actual map page (Leaflet.js + OpenStreetMap tiles, plus a static undersea-cable reference layer) lives in the baltic-monitor-site repo -- see that repo own README. 25 new tests (567 -> 592).

recent_updates.title: New: /satellite -- raw Sentinel-2 imagery, deliberately no ML interpretation
recent_updates.text: Added /satellite <site>, sending a real, recent, best-effort cloud-free true-color Sentinel-2 photo (free Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem imagery) of a named site -- Baltiysk, Chkalovsk, Pskov, or Luga -- straight to the private chat, exactly as received. Deliberately does NOT do what a dead but more advanced competitor, estwarden.eu, used to: run ML object detection to call a garrison 'empty' or 'occupied'. A false automated claim about troop movements would cost this project the trust it depends on, so that interpretation step is a considered non-feature, not a gap -- the caption says so outright. On-demand only, permanently -- no scan-time scoring, no baseline, no alerting.

recent_updates.title: Fixed a silent /firms send failure (unescaped underscores broke Telegram Markdown)
recent_updates.text: Found and fixed a real bug: format_firms_status()'s static caveat text contained unescaped underscores (VIIRS_SNPP_NRT, MAP_KEY, FIRMS_MAP_KEY) that Telegram's legacy Markdown parser reads as italic-toggle characters -- an odd total count fails the ENTIRE message with a silent HTTP 400 the job never surfaces (send_telegram() only logs an [ERROR] and continues), so a real /firms check could 'succeed' with nothing actually delivered. Backslash-escaped the static identifiers and added a Markdown-balance regression test so this class of bug fails CI next time, not a live run. Also stopped the firms_status CLI dispatch from printing a confident 'sent' line regardless of whether the send actually worked.

recent_updates.title: /notam now covers Estonia too (Phase 1 + 2)
recent_updates.text: Extended /notam beyond Latvia: found that EANS (Estonia's Aeronautical Information Service) publishes a free, unauthenticated JSON NOTAM feed (aim.eans.ee) -- confirmed live before writing any parsing code, separate from the interactive self-briefing tool that blocked this earlier. Already structured data, so no ICAO field-letter parsing needed the way Latvia's HTML feed requires. Both /notam and its automatic-scan new-military-NOTAM check now cover Estonia and Latvia, tracked independently so one country's feed having a bad day can't corrupt the other's baseline. Lithuania remains a real, stated gap (ans.lt blocks automated access, same as /notmar). 19 new tests (516 -> 535).

recent_updates.title: NASA FIRMS thermal hotspot tracking (/firms)
recent_updates.text: Added /firms: on-demand satellite thermal-anomaly detection for the Baltic region via NASA FIRMS (VIIRS, near-real-time, free with a self-service MAP_KEY), closing a real gap -- this project had no fire/thermal monitoring at all, even though it's an established OSINT signal for spotting explosions, large fires, and unusual military/industrial activity. Same two-phase pattern as /gpsjam, /ais, /military, /notam: Phase 1 on-demand command, Phase 2 silent per-scan snapshot with a WATCH/WARN deviation context line, never a standalone trigger. Stated plainly in every reply: this is raw satellite heat data, NOT confirmed military activity -- wildfires, agricultural burning, and industrial flares trigger it just as readily. Requires a free FIRMS_MAP_KEY secret; replies "not configured" until it's set. 28 new tests (488 -> 516).

recent_updates.title: Fixed: mute-list false negative and a GDELT accounting bug
recent_updates.text: Full-project sweep found two real bugs: the wildlife mute list was silently dropping unrelated real stories ("boar" matched inside "boarding" -- e.g. vessel-interdiction stories; "hare" matched inside "shared") due to substring rather than whole-word matching, now fixed. Separately, GDELT's deliberate quota-throttle skip was being counted the same as a real failure, which silently broke quiet mode's QUIET-scan suppression and inflated the GDELT failure count shown in the daily report and public status page -- now tracked correctly as a skip, not a failure.

recent_updates.title: New OSINT sources for military tracking
recent_updates.text: Added Bellingcat and TWZ (The War Zone) as Tier 3 sources — specialist outlets that verify military exercises and equipment movements from open-source evidence, closing out the last piece of Baltic Signal Monitor's force-posture tracking (after aircraft and ship tracking). These stay in the lowest-confidence tier, same as all Tier 3 sources, never counted as confirmation on their own.

recent_updates.title: AIS now flags self-declared military/law-enforcement vessels
recent_updates.text: Extended /ais and its automatic scan check to read a vessel's own self-declared ship type (a standard AIS field), flagging any that identify as Military, Law Enforcement, or Noncombatant. Deliberately not based on a curated list of specific ships -- only on what each vessel's own transponder broadcasts, honestly caveated since most vessels won't show a type in any single snapshot.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: GDELT Cloud enrichment was silently capped for half of every month
recent_updates.text: Found the real cause of the recent GDELT Cloud failures: the free plan's 100-request monthly quota, burned through by this project's own usage in about half the month. Cut the automatic scan's GDELT Cloud calls from 6x/day to 3x/day so the free quota now lasts the full month. Map pins and severity scores on flagged items will be a bit less frequent, but core detection was never affected either way.

recent_updates.title: Baltic Notices to Mariners tracking (/notmar)
recent_updates.text: Added /notmar: on-demand check of Estonia's and Latvia's official Notices to Mariners bulletins, filtered to security-relevant activity (military exercises, submarine cable/pipeline notices, restricted zones). Same informational-only pattern as /gpsjam, /ais, and /military -- never triggers an alert on its own. Lithuania isn't covered yet; its official site blocks automated access, the same gap /notam already has.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: scheduled health checks were wasting GitHub Actions minutes
recent_updates.text: The automated twice-daily health check was re-checking every single source the same expensive way a full scan does, even though a much cheaper check already covers what it needs to catch. This was quietly using roughly half of this project's free monthly automation budget for no real benefit -- fixed with no change to scan frequency or freshness.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: WATCH/WARN digests could silently fail to send to Telegram
recent_updates.text: Some real alerts' full digest message (the one with the actual headline and link) could silently never reach the channel, depending on which signal categories matched -- caused by an unescaped Markdown character in how categories were listed. Only the shorter summary message was reliably getting through. Category names now display as plain text (e.g. 'nato conflict risk') which fixes the underlying cause for every case, not just the one that surfaced it.

recent_updates.title: NOTAM messages now plain-language, not raw aviation codes
recent_updates.text: The /notam command (and the automatic scan context that uses the same data) used to show raw ICAO NOTAM shorthand -- field codes and aviation abbreviations that aren't meaningful without training. It now translates that into plain sentences with normal dates.

recent_updates.title: AIS, military aircraft, and Latvia NOTAM now feed automatic scans
recent_updates.text: These three checks used to be on-demand only (Telegram commands you had to trigger yourself). Now they run automatically as part of every scan: if a scan already flags WATCH or WARN from the normal news scoring, unusual ship or aircraft activity or a newly-published military NOTAM gets added as extra context on that alert. None of the three can trigger an alert by themselves -- this project never lets one source alone do that.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: chart tone direction and 1D-1Y range selector scale
recent_updates.text: The escalation-intensity chart's tone axis was backwards (worse plotted lower); flipped so higher now always means worse. The 1D/1W/1M/6M/1Y range buttons also now actually rescale the chart to the selected window instead of always stretching whatever data exists to fill the full width. History window bumped from ~33 days to ~1 year to support the longer ranges.

recent_updates.title: New: /notam command -- Latvia military-activity NOTAM tracking (Phase 1)
recent_updates.text: Added a fourth on-demand check alongside GPSJam/AIS/military: current NOTAMs (official aviation notices) from Latvia's national Aeronautical Information Service, filtered to ones mentioning military activity -- restricted airspace activations, parachute exercises, and similar. Checkable any time via the Telegram bot. Latvia only for now; Estonia and Lithuania coverage may follow. Same design as the other three: informational only, never triggers an alert on its own, no API key needed.

recent_updates.title: New: escalation-intensity and rumor-tracking charts
recent_updates.text: Two new charts on the site's Track Record section: one showing escalation intensity over time (GDELT coverage tone, plus each scan colored by its actual QUIET/WATCH/WARN result), and one showing rumor/disinformation tracking volume over time. Builds on today's fix to how rumors are detected, so the rumor chart now reflects real activity instead of a filter that was silently missing most of it.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: rumor/disinfo tracking was silently missing most real content
recent_updates.text: The Tier 3 rumor/disinformation digest was using the same strict relevance filter built for mainstream news, which required an unrelated second category on top of being Baltic-specific -- but Tier 3 sources are already curated to be Baltic/Russia disinfo content, so this was silently dropping the vast majority of genuinely on-topic reporting (a live check found only 2 of 184 fetched items passing). Fixed with a dedicated, appropriately looser check for this tier, while adding a new guard against a separate junk-data issue the same check surfaced. Never affects WATCH/WARN scoring -- Tier 3 still can't trigger an alert on its own.

recent_updates.title: New: /military command -- live military aircraft snapshot (Phase 1)
recent_updates.text: Added a third on-demand check alongside GPSJam/AIS: a live snapshot of military aircraft in the Baltic region via adsb.lol's free, unfiltered ADS-B feed, checkable any time via the Telegram bot. Same design as the other two -- informational only, never triggers an alert on its own, and clearly states it only sees aircraft actively broadcasting (many military flights don't). First of three planned phases in a broader force-posture tracking effort; naval and OSINT-tracker phases are next.

recent_updates.title: Clearer explanations: QUIET/WATCH/WARN, tiers, and what the map shows
recent_updates.text: Added a plain-language guide to the pinned channel message and every map post explaining what QUIET/WATCH/WARN mean, what the source tiers are, and -- important -- that the on-demand map shows raw, unfiltered background data where most dots are NOT security alerts. Also added a matching FAQ entry on the site explaining the GDELT/Goldstein detail shown on some items.

recent_updates.title: Fixed broken WATCH/WARN map images
recent_updates.text: The map attached to WATCH/WARN alerts was sometimes showing blocked placeholder tiles instead of a real map, due to a tile-server policy change on our end. Switched to a different map provider built for this -- maps should now render correctly every time.

recent_updates.title: New: live AIS ship-tracking snapshot for the Baltic (on demand)
recent_updates.text: Added a second on-demand check alongside the GPS-jamming one: a short live snapshot of ship positions in the Baltic Sea via aisstream.io's free AIS feed, checkable any time via the Telegram bot. Same design as the jamming check -- informational only, a brief listen-window snapshot rather than exhaustive tracking, never triggers an alert on its own, and the underlying service is an explicit public beta, stated plainly in the reply.

recent_updates.title: GPS jamming data now part of the picture
recent_updates.text: Added GPSJam.org's crowdsourced Baltic GPS-jamming data as a new information layer. Owners can check the current picture on demand any time via the Telegram bot; and when this system's own sources already flag a WATCH or WARN, a short note is now added if that day's jamming is meaningfully above or below its recent normal level. Unofficial, crowdsourced data -- never triggers an alert on its own, always shown with a caveat and a link to the source.

recent_updates.title: VSquare and Atlantic Council DFRLab added, a duplicate source fixed
recent_updates.text: Added two more sources: VSquare, a Central European investigative journalism network tracking Russian military buildup along the NATO border, and Atlantic Council's DFRLab, whose reporting has used satellite imagery to identify Russian troop buildups. Also fixed a duplicate: Bellingcat had accidentally been added twice under the same name, now merged into one entry with the better-performing query. Now tracking 131 sources.

recent_updates.title: Bellingcat added as a source
recent_updates.text: Added Bellingcat, the respected investigative OSINT outlet, to Tier 2 — its coverage of GRU Unit 29155 (the clandestine sabotage unit behind the Skripal poisoning and multiple European destabilization operations) is directly relevant to the hybrid incidents this project tracks. Now tracking 130 sources.

recent_updates.title: Denmark, Netherlands, and EEAS added as source countries
recent_updates.text: Added six more sources: Denmark's Defence Intelligence Service, Ministry of Defence, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the Netherlands' AIVD (intelligence service) and Ministry of Defence; and EEAS, the EU's foreign-policy arm behind the EUvsDisinfo project. Denmark controls the Baltic Sea straits and the Netherlands' AIVD has published detailed reporting on Russian sabotage-network activity — both are a strong fit for this project's early-warning mission specifically. Same rule as every other source: counts as evidence only when a story actually names a Baltic country or flashpoint. Now tracking 129 sources.

recent_updates.title: USA, UK, and Germany added as source countries
recent_updates.text: Added nine sources across the US, UK, and Germany — each country's public-facing intelligence/security body (US ODNI, UK NCSC, German BfV), defence and foreign ministries (US DoD/State, UK MOD, German BMVg/Federal Foreign Office), and Germany's leading security think tank (SWP) — following the same source-only approach already used for Poland: these count as evidence only when a story actually names a Baltic country or flashpoint, not for every Russia-related story from these sources. Now tracking 123 sources.
